bug_semantics: Authenticated users remain inside their configured filesystem scope but can bypass administrator path deny rules because authorization compares the uncanonicalized virtual path literally while the backing filesystem resolves an equivalent name differently. On case-insensitive filesystems, a case variant such as /secret.TXT names denied /Secret.txt without matching its case-sensitive rule. On Windows, a mixed-separator traversal such as /allow\..\Secret.txt likewise misses the slash-based rule while filepath/afero resolves it to the denied file. The affected operations include reads and, subject to the user's ordinary permissions, modification, deletion, copying, and sharing; internally generated OS-separated paths also caused nested recursive/archive checks to miss rules on Windows.
flaw_origin: The recoverable pre-squash PR history is two-stage. Commit 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c first wrote the flawed path-rule primitive: User.IsAllowed uses raw, case-sensitive strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path), while User.BuildFs exposes the scope through afero.NewBasePathFs and therefore host filesystem path semantics. Commit 41828f18050c3e90fc54ea2468324246b45e7d85 then activated that primitive at the HTTP resource gate and directory-listing checks. The smallest source-level flaw origin is 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c; later moves through types/rule.go, lib/rule.go, rules/rules.go, and master squash 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 preserve rather than originate it.
ai_marker: absent — BIC commit object has no AI author/co-author/Generated-with marker; see evidence
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-fgm5-pw99-w2p7 states that rules.Rule.Matches compared raw paths literally, data.Check passed through the received path, case variants bypassed rules on case-insensitive filesystems, Windows backslashes were resolved by afero/filepath but not by the rule checker, affected versions were <=2.63.20, and v2.63.21/#6045 fixed the issue.

The historical PR #575 timeline at https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/pull/575 exposes the force-push comparison https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/compare/2f08d7cd9af287b9cc7a577357993fd65761bf7e..72753107876da63326250c3501eb5c291fb3e207. In a temporary bare clone, `git fetch --no-tags https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser.git 2f08d7cd9af287b9cc7a577357993fd65761bf7e` recovers the pre-squash member history; both 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c and 41828f18050c3e90fc54ea2468324246b45e7d85 are ancestors of that tip. `git diff 2f08d7cd9af287b9cc7a577357993fd65761bf7e 72753107876da63326250c3501eb5c291fb3e207 -- types/user.go types/rule.go http/resource.go` is empty, confirming that the force-pushed aggregate retained the relevant authorization code.

On the recovered history, `git log -L :IsAllowed:types/user.go 2f08d7cd9af287b9cc7a577357993fd65761bf7e` traces the vulnerable function to 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c. `git show 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c -- types/user.go` shows that commit adding User.Rules, host-backed afero.NewBasePathFs, and the literal `strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path)` decision. The independent pickaxe `git log ... -S'strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path)' -- types/user.go` selects the same member commit rather than the later public squash.

Direct parent verification: `git cat-file -p 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c` names sole parent 8e6e2119db14d33b56fc2dff13e0cf7c99439438, and `git grep -n -F 'strings.HasPrefix(url, rule.Path)' 8e6e2119db14d33b56fc2dff13e0cf7c99439438 -- '*.go'` has no match. `git show 41828f18050c3e90fc54ea2468324246b45e7d85 -- http/resource.go types/files.go` then shows the raw path being passed to user.IsAllowed before resource access and for directory entries, establishing the activation step without changing the flawed matcher.

The public master history obscures these members in aggregate commit 12b2c215221696de58431093e01eeff7a5414471 (`feat: v2 (#599)`): `git log -S'func (r *Rule) Matches(path string)' -- rules/rules.go` finds that aggregate. It is rejected as the BIC because the PR timeline and fetchable pre-force-push objects decompose the relevant logic to 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c plus activation commit 41828f18050c3e90fc54ea2468324246b45e7d85.

Version boundary: `git show v2.0.0:rules/rules.go` and `git show v2.0.0:http/data.go` show the raw case-sensitive matcher and unchecked path handoff in the first v2 release (tag target e706391934d79ceca7f639eccda96df4dec55f48). `git show v2.63.20:rules/rules.go` still has the literal matcher (tag target 50125a5d21c9f5e9a78db80d77a26139614ce72e). `git log v2.63.20..v2.63.21` identifies e6d70cf24c0cd79a1787601dc99104ec7e7ca3ef as `fix(http): canonicalize paths before checking access rules (#6045)`, and the v2.63.21 release commit f6fb8f6bf52d714b2215534033a3c96316069efc has that fix as its immediate parent.

Fix verification: `git show e6d70cf24c0cd79a1787601dc99104ec7e7ca3ef` adds host-separator canonicalization before every rule decision, canonicalizes external request/query paths, detects whether the backing root is case-insensitive, and passes that fact to Rule.Matches so non-regex path rules fold case only when appropriate. This directly closes both path-equivalence forms described by the advisory.

BIC-only AI check: raw `git cat-file -p 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c` shows author and committer `Henrique Dias <hacdias@gmail.com>`, timestamp 2018-11-29, and the sole message `more permissions and remove user.Check`; it contains no AI Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker. No signal from the fix or later commits was used for the verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the semantic disagreement between literal rule matching and host filesystem path equivalence, not a later refactor or the 2026 fix. The earliest recoverable member that wrote that flawed decision is 3dcbdfc8776b25f58a9134ba9f4d893f62db2b7c, and its direct parent lacks the decision. The following member 41828f18050c3e90fc54ea2468324246b45e7d85 makes the flawed helper security-relevant by putting it on the resource and listing paths; both were later hidden by force-push/squash history but remain publicly fetchable and reproducible. Equivalent code shipped from v2.0.0 through v2.63.20, and direct fix e6d70cf24c0cd79a1787601dc99104ec7e7ca3ef landed immediately before the v2.63.21 release. Because the BIC commit object is a human-authored 2018 commit with no AI marker, the protocol requires NOT_AI.
